schemes.official_name: Vertically Integrated Projects for Sustainable Development (VIP4SD)
schemes.english_name: Vertically Integrated Projects for Sustainable Development
schemes.description: Multidisciplinary, multi-year, credit-bearing research/challenge projects addressing the UN SDGs. Teams combine students from different year groups and disciplines with academics and postgraduate researchers; individual projects (e.g. Energy for Development solar PV installations, STEM education in primary schools, Drug Discovery) work with collaborators such as local schools, the NHS and partners in Malawi, Rwanda and the Gambia. Whether external organisations are a standard source of the brief for every project is not evidenced.
schemes.admin_host: Centre for Sustainable Development / VIP4SD programme
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Projects across all four faculties (being introduced across all four faculties per Nov 2025 strategy); eligibility and credit values said to be listed on the programme site but not retrieved.
schemes.year_of_study: From second year to Honours and beyond (multi-year)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Students in participating degrees and project teams; credit depends on degree.
schemes.credit_assessment: Academic credit towards degree (value not retrieved).
schemes.project_evidence: Research/challenge projects with defined SDG-related aims and outputs (e.g. solar PV installations, school STEM teaching) [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Teams of students from different year groups and disciplines work collaboratively with staff and postgraduate researchers [1][2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Individual projects work with schools, NHS and overseas partners [2][3], but the source does not show external organisations setting the brief or taking part as client for each project; roles of partners (beneficiary vs client) not documented. Coverage 'some projects'.
schemes.partner_role: Collaborators/beneficiaries on individual projects (schools, NHS, overseas institutions); programme-level partners include Scottish Government, Royal Academy of Engineering, EAUC.
schemes.named_partners: Local schools, NHS, partners in Malawi, Rwanda and the Gambia (undated programme pages)
schemes.deliverable: Project outputs (e.g. installations, teaching interventions, research outputs)
schemes.participation_data: Approx. 200 students across 20 interdisciplinary research projects (University sustainability strategy case study, SESS30, Nov 2025 document).
schemes.unresolved: Credit value per project, eligibility, and whether external organisations set briefs or only benefit. Participation figures are from an undated case study within a Nov 2025 document.

schemes.official_name: DMEM Industrial Group Projects (IGP) / Industrial Projects scheme
schemes.english_name: Design, Manufacturing & Engineering Management Industrial Group Projects
schemes.description: Team-based industrial project in which a company sets an outline brief (agreed in preliminary discussions), and a team of senior undergraduate and postgraduate taught students (single- or multi-discipline) manages the project through four stages (Brief, Definition, Conceptualisation, Realisation) to a product, system or process solution, usually with a report and sometimes prototype/CAD/data. Each team has a university mentor and a client representative; the client gives formal feedback at each milestone and attends the presentation day. Evidenced on the MSc Systems Engineering Management page as a 40-credit module with report and presentation to the client (past clients listed: Babcock, BAE Systems, Rolls-Royce, Thales, Jacobs).
schemes.admin_host: Department of Design, Manufacturing & Engineering Management (Faculty of Engineering)
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Senior undergraduate and postgraduate taught students on DMEM product design, manufacture and engineering management related degrees (e.g. MEng Manufacturing Engineering with Management, MSc Systems Engineering Management, Product Design Engineering).
schemes.credit_assessment: 40-credit module on MSc Systems Engineering Management (course page); BEng assessment: brief and report/folio 75%, critiques 25% (per search summary). Credit values on other programmes not confirmed.
schemes.duration: October to May; January to August
schemes.delivery_format: In-person team projects with client liaison; presentation day in May/August
schemes.project_evidence: Defined client brief, four staged milestones, final report/prototype/CAD/data [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: 'Team-based industrial project'; project allocated to a team of single- or multi-discipline students [1][2][3].
schemes.employer_evidence: Company sets the brief, nominates a representative, gives formal feedback at each stage and is expected to attend the presentation day [1][2]; MSc SEM students present to the client [3].
schemes.partner_role: Client company sets brief, liaises, gives milestone feedback, attends presentation day.
schemes.named_partners: Babcock, BAE Systems, Rolls-Royce, Thales, Jacobs (SEM course page, undated); Rolls-Royce, Unilever, Jaguar Land Rover, NHS listed as companies worked with (DMEM page); Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh in 2021-22 catalogue
schemes.deliverable: Report, often with prototype, CAD layouts or experimental data; client presentation
schemes.unresolved: Credit values and compulsory status per programme beyond MSc SEM; no 2025/26 cohort list found (dated evidence is the May 2025 presentation day record).

profile_md:
**Strathclyde has several distributed, programme-embedded client-project routes, concentrated in Engineering and the Business School, plus a university-wide VIP4SD framework whose partner role is unclear.**

The clearest route is the Design, Manufacturing & Engineering Management (DMEM) Industrial Group Projects: companies set outline briefs, teams of senior undergraduate and postgraduate taught students work through four client-reviewed stages to a report or prototype, and the client attends the May/August presentation day (a 9 May 2025 presentation day is recorded). It is a compulsory element within DMEM programmes (40 credits on MSc Systems Engineering Management). The MSc Civil Engineering group design project (20 credits) adds industry mentors such as Arcadis and Skanska but lacks dated currency evidence.

In Strathclyde Business School, the MSc Business Analysis & Consulting class (Becoming an Effective Business Analyst) has allocated teams solving client problems; a March 2026 newsletter names Deloitte, StormID, Sphera and WB Alloys. Team consultancy modules also appear in BA Business Analysis & Technology, Marketing Works (an option on MSc Marketing) and Consultancy in Practice, but are evidenced only by undated pages.

VIP4SD gives credit-bearing multi-year teams across faculties (about 200 students, 20 projects), but external partners appear as collaborators on some projects rather than documented clients. Entrepreneurship challenges, the Law Clinic (individual public clients), summer consultancy projects and Careers pages were excluded. Further departmental capstones (computing, mechanical, Honours projects) likely exist but lack separable evidence.
gaps: Most Business School and Civil Engineering pages are undated (some roughly a decade old), so current delivery is unconfirmed for S3, S5-S9. Credit values, compulsory status and assessment splits are missing for several routes. Further departmental instances likely (Honours client projects, Management Science 4, computing/mechanical group projects, Education, Product Design). VIP4SD partner roles and eligibility/credit not retrieved. Architecture scheme wording may blend with DMEM wording.
